thread:
Alex W: kicking off quiet window now for the tf apply to roll out the vpc/iam changes in us-west-2. plan looked clean on the preflight, tagging infra and oncall.
Maria P: putting links here: https://git.internal/repo/changes/422 and tfplan: https://ci.internal/plan/422. added release notes snippet to the PR.
Deploybot: ⚙️ queued terraform apply #422 by Alex W (workspace: prod-usw2). expected duration ~8m. will emit events.
Raj K: quick reminder — this adds an iam role binding for analytics-service. if anyone's testing with service tokens, double-check.
SRE Lead: canary policy: start at 10% traffic for 15m, if error-rate > 2% or latency P95 regresses > 150ms then rollback. ops oncall alerted.
Alex W: acknowledged. I'll pin provider to hash to avoid drift (provider v3.2.1). committing the pin now.
Maria P: commit pushed with provider pin and a tfvar to gate the role creation: `create_analytics_role = true`. PR: https://git.internal/repo/pr/789
Alex W: running the apply command now:
```
terraform apply -auto-approve -target=module.network -var-file=prod-usw2.tfvars
```
Ops Oncall: if apply stalls or plan changes unexpectedly, abort and call rollback: `deploybot rollback --apply-id 422` and open the incident channel.
Deploybot: apply started (id=422). streaming logs to https://ci.internal/logs/422. eta 7m.
Raj K: saw the iam binding change in the plan output, looks correct. no existing policy references the new role. :thumbsup:
SRE Lead: first 5m canary looks green. increasing to 50% traffic for 30m as a progressive step.
Maria P: updated release notes with the rollback procedure and version pin details. also added the changelog entry: "pin provider to v3.2.1; add analytics-service IAM role behind gate"
Alex W: apply completed, outputs show new vpc subnets and role ARN. marking canary in progress.
SRE Lead: metrics stable at 50% for 10m. continuing runway to full rollout.
Ops Oncall: leaving rollback window open until EOD per policy in case downstream jobs need time. ping me if we need to revert.
Alex W: thanks everyone — closing thread when we hit full rollout and stability window.
